title: Goal node
description: One node of the goal tree (PLAN §2, Q3). Runs attach to nodes; budgets live per node; the drift governor fires on budget breach -> auto-strategy-review. The tree is stored one-file-per-node (parent pointers), so the dashboard rebuilds the tree from the node set; this is git-friendlier than one monolithic tree file. The thesis root has parent=null and is_trunk_artifact=true (the gap / thesis contribution that papers can threaten and meetings can steer, Q10).

id.description: goal_<kebab-slug>. Stable; runs, contracts and child nodes reference it.

node_kind.description: Depth in the tree. thesis = root (one). chapter = major thrust. branch = a contracted line of work. question = a specific answerable question runs attach to.

parent.description: Parent goal_node id. Null ONLY for the thesis root.

state.description: open = active. blocked = waiting on a dependency. closed = done/abandoned. revivable = closed but its blocker may no longer hold (dead-branch revival scans these, PLAN §4).

budget.description: Expected cost. The governor compares spent vs this (breach factor is config, PLAN §7.2, not in-schema).

expected_wall_s.description: Expected total compute wall in seconds.

spent.description: Accumulated actuals (summed from child_runs by the indexer).

contract_refs.description: branch_contract ids attached to this node (a branch usually has one frozen contract; amendments live inside it).

child_runs.description: run_record ids attached directly to this node. (Child NODES are discovered via their parent pointer, not listed here.)

last_measured.description: The most recent headline result on this node — what 'Last measured' lines in PROGRESS currently encode by hand.

run.description: run_record id of the measuring run.

is_trunk_artifact.description: True for the gap / thesis-contribution node (Q10): a first-class trunk artifact papers can threaten and meetings can steer. Typically exactly one node carries this.
